title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
claim: High-nuclearity lanthanide hydroxide clusters are assembled from a small set of recurring polyhedra—triangular {Ln3(μ3-OH)}, cubane {Ln4(μ3-OH)4}, trigonal-bipyramidal {Ln5(μ3-OH)6}, square-pyramidal {Ln5(μ3-OH)4(μ4-O)} and octahedral {Ln6(μ6-O)(μ3-OH)8}—by vertex-, edge- or face-sharing, often of more than one motif.
explanation: The introduction states that even structurally diverse clusters contain these basic motifs and that sophisticated cores combine two or more of them. Section 3 and Figs. 16–21 then map representative nuclearities onto edge- or vertex-sharing of triangles, vertex-sharing cubanes, corner-sharing square pyramids or octahedra, and mixed-motif cores.
scope: Lanthanide hydroxide cluster cores from small oligomers through Ln104, including some heterometallic examples such as Zn4@Ln24.
caveats: Some figure captions use the word square pyramid for {Ln5(μ3-OH)6}, whereas the text and Fig. 16 assign that formula to the trigonal bipyramid and {Ln5(μ3-OH)4(μ4-O)} to the square pyramid; the textual assignment is the consistent one.
